column1: The factors emphasized in this chapter—central bank preferences, the short-run real e¤ects of surprise inflation, the rate at which the central bank discounts the future, the e¤ects of political influences on the central bank—are quite di¤erent from the factors that received prominence in the optimal taxation models of inflation of chapter 4. Although a large number of empirical studies of the industrialized economies have found that indices of central bank political independence are negatively related to average inflation, evidence also suggests the importance of financing considerations.
